answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a jade as the anchor of the cost.
